_comment: One person, one key. Hand-edited: nothing on disk can decide these, and
core/aliases.py says what was measured and rejected before it came to a
`name` is the PERFORMING name and becomes the key every credit
accumulates under -- it is what listens.artist_key carries, so the 59%
hit-rate measurement still joins, and it is the name a reader knows.
`also` is every other spelling seen in a walked corpus. `why` and
`seen_on` are for the next reader; nothing reads them.
Only pairs somebody checked. `stages/discover.py` prints the candidates
it did NOT merge at the end of a walk, including the ones it calls
`bare` -- a single surname like "Massey" or "Glennie", which is the
collision class that is 47% of the candidate pool. Read those before
